# Strategy seed: Avery and Jordan Sample

We are Avery and Jordan Sample. We file married filing jointly and live in Laramie County, Wyoming, so we have no state income tax. We are preparing our TY_2025 federal return and would like help getting it right, and checking that our earlier returns hold up.

## Our situation

- Two W-2 jobs. Avery's employer, Northwind Example Corp., pays part of Avery's pay in RSUs that vest each March. Jordan works at Harborline Example Inc.
- We keep a taxable brokerage account at Brightfield Example Brokerage LLC and have sold some funds at a loss in the past.
- We bought our first home in July 2024.
- We filed 2022 on extension in October 2023. We have not looked at the older returns since.

## What we believe about capital losses

We had a big capital loss in 2022 and carried the rest forward. Our understanding is that the capital loss limit is $3,000 per spouse, so $6,000 for us, and we have been planning around deducting up to $6,000 of losses against wages each year.

- "Claim for credit or refund of an overpayment of any tax imposed by this title"
- "shall be filed by the taxpayer within 3 years from the time the return was filed"
- "or 2 years from the time the tax was paid, whichever of such periods expires the later"
- "or if no return was filed by the taxpayer, within 2 years from the time the tax was paid."

**§ 6511(b)(2)(A): Limit where claim filed within 3-year period**

- "If the claim was filed by the taxpayer during the 3-year period prescribed in subsection (a),"
- "the amount of the credit or refund shall not exceed the portion of the tax paid within the period,"
- "immediately preceding the filing of the claim, equal to 3 years plus the period of any extension"
- "of time for filing the return."

**§ 6511(b)(2)(B): Limit where claim not filed within 3-year period**

- "If the claim was not filed within such 3-year period, the amount of the credit or refund shall not exceed"
- "the portion of the tax paid during the 2 years immediately preceding the filing of the claim."

**§ 6511(h): Suspension while financially disabled**

- "the running of the periods specified in subsections (a), (b), and (c) shall be suspended"
- "during any period of such individual’s life that such individual is financially disabled."
